claims.text: WTaTiVZr is an equimolar high-entropy alloy.
The multiple principal elements in WTaTiVZr inherently introduce lattice distortions.
The lattice distortions in WTaTiVZr expand or spread dislocation cores.
Dislocation-core spreading reduces the Peierls barrier in WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
A wider dislocation core reduces the critical resolved shear stress required for dislocation motion.
Pure tungsten has a more uniform lattice than WTaTiVZr.
The proposed Peierls-barrier reduction facilitates dislocation glide at lower applied stress in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten.
Facilitated dislocation glide enhances the plastic strain of WTaTiVZr under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service conditions.
Facilitated dislocation glide enhances the toughness of WTaTiVZr under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service conditions.
The controlled comparison uses WTaTiVZr and commercially pure tungsten under identical high-temperature testing conditions.
The proposed tests combine validated-potential atomistic simulations with high-temperature nanoindentation in an inert atmosphere.
The proposed service-relevant temperature range is 800–1100 °C.
Simulations are predicted to show more diffuse dislocation cores in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten.
Simulations are predicted to show lower critical resolved shear stress in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten.
Nanoindentation is predicted to show smoother load-displacement curves and fewer pop-in events for WTaTiVZr than for pure tungsten.
Reduced pop-in activity and smoother indentation curves indicate enhanced plastic-deformation capability.
The proposed nanoindentation observations indicate higher toughness in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten.
The hypothesis may cease to govern deformation when grain-boundary segregation, precipitation, or other mechanisms dominate.

contradictions.description: The phrase "as-cast ... with homogenized microstructures" conflates an as-cast condition with a homogenized condition unless homogenization refers only to controlled microstructural matching; the actual processing state is therefore internally ambiguous.
